title: Applied Artificial Intelligence in Business
overview: Additional business major combining applied AI, responsible use, two business electives and a choice of Disruptive Tech or Machine Learning focus. The 33-credit inventory includes 15 credits in the required primary business major.

courses.name: Introduction to Applied Artificial Intelligence
courses.description: Introduces applied-AI technologies, programming tools, business problem solving, and responsible technology use.
courses.prerequisites: Enrolled in the College of Business, BUAD 1001 and BUAD 1560 (only BUAD 1560 can be taken concurrently); or BUAN minor and COMM 1700 , MATH 1700 , MATH 4710 , MATH 4720 , MATH 4740 , MEEN 3426 , SOCI 2060 or SOCI 2060H .

category_review.rationale: Applied-AI technologies are central, with introductory programming and ethics serving that stated goal.

courses.name: Application of AI/ML in Finance and Beyond
courses.description: Applies machine-learning and AI models to finance and broader corporate decisions.

category_review.rationale: The description explicitly focuses on ML/AI models and techniques, rather than finance alone.

courses.name: Data-Driven Marketing: Analytics, Insights and Applied AI
courses.description: Integrates AI, machine learning, and data-science tools into marketing decisions and customer engagement.
courses.prerequisites: MARK 3001 and BUAD 1560 (or COMM 1700 , MATH 1700 , MATH 4720 or SOCI 2060 for non-business students).

category_review.rationale: Specific AI/ML and data-science techniques are the central analytic tools described.

courses.name: Artificial Intelligence in Supply Chain
courses.description: Applies AI and machine learning to forecasting, inventory, logistics, warehouses, and supplier decisions.

category_review.rationale: Machine-learning and AI-powered decision systems are central stated methods.

courses.name: Ethics, Governance, and Responsible Use in AI
courses.description: Studies ethical implications, governance, risk, transparency, and accountability in organizational AI deployment.
courses.prerequisites: Completed the Disruptive Tech focus or the Machine Learning focus of the Major in Applied AI, BUAD 2001 , Sr. stndg.

category_review.rationale: Ethics, governance and responsible social/organizational deployment form the subject rather than model construction.

courses.name: FinTech Foundations and Applications
courses.description: Builds financial-technology business concepts using AI tools, automation, APIs, and machine-learning bots.
courses.prerequisites: FINA 3001 , which may be taken concurrently; or BUAD 2001 ; or cons. of instr.

category_review.rationale: The experiential course combines pitching/valuation and multiple technologies to produce financial applications; AI is one tool within the domain project.

courses.name: Identifying, Building, Creating and Communicating FinTech Opportunities
courses.description: Identifies and communicates financial-technology opportunities across AI, digital assets, contracts, and blockchain.
courses.prerequisites: FINA 4075 or FINA 5075 which may be taken concurrently; AIM major; or cons. of instr.

category_review.rationale: FinTech opportunity analysis spans several technologies, with AI as one of them; financial application is the common subject.

courses.name: Leveraging AI with Predictive Analytics
courses.description: Builds predictive business models using regression, decision trees, clustering, and time-series methods.
courses.prerequisites: Enrolled in the College of Business and BUAD 1560 ; or BUAN minor and COMM 1700 , MATH 1700 , MATH 4710 , MATH 4720 , MATH 4740 , MEEN 3426 , SOCI 2060 or SOCI 2060H .

category_review.rationale: Machine-learning model design and implementation are explicit primary activities.

courses.name: Harnessing the Decision-Making Power of AI with Prescriptive Analytics
courses.description: Uses optimization, simulation, heuristics, and prescriptive analytical methods for business decisions.

category_review.rationale: The description centers on mathematical optimization and simulation; the AI title alone does not establish AI methods.

requirements.title: Primary business major required
requirements.summary: This is an additional major paired with an eligible primary major in the College of Business Administration.

requirements.title: Major course grades
requirements.summary: All major requirements and electives, including introductory core courses, require C or higher. Credit is not awarded twice for a repeated course except distinct variable-topic sections.

requirements.title: Eligible primary majors
requirements.summary: Pair with accounting, business economics, finance, human resources, information systems, marketing, operations and supply chain management, or real estate. Business administration does not permit a second business major.

requirements.title: Credit sharing across business majors
requirements.summary: Requirements and upper-division electives may be shared across majors, with at least 30 upper-division credits for two majors. Sharing never reduces degree credit totals.

requirements.title: International business content
requirements.summary: At least one course with international business content is required, within or outside the declared business majors.

requirements.title: Declaration and major limit
requirements.summary: Students should declare before senior-year advising and registration; a maximum of three business majors is permitted.

requirements.title: Major GPA
requirements.summary: The major requires a GPA of at least 2.000.

requirements.title: Major residence
requirements.summary: At least half of major credits must be completed at Marquette; degree-wide residency rules also apply.

requirements.title: University major declaration and residence
requirements.summary: Only degree-seeking students may declare; Business students must declare before junior year. The current curriculum at declaration normally applies. At least 15 major credits must be completed at Marquette.

requirements.title: Major courses cannot use CR/NC
requirements.summary: CR/NC is restricted to general electives; it cannot satisfy major requirements.

requirements.title: Course access and completion sequence
requirements.summary: INSY 4180 requires completion of either focus, BUAD 2001, and senior standing. AIM 4410 lists FINA 4075 or FINA 5075 (may be concurrent), AIM-major status, or instructor consent; the additional-major route does not imply consent. Individual business course prerequisites remain on the course records.

notes: Additional major; the primary business major determines the bachelor degree. The 33 credits are not 33 additional credits on top of the primary major.

University policy requires declaration before junior year; college guidance encourages early declaration and recommends all declarations before senior-year advising. Both source statements are retained.

All nine named course descriptions and prerequisites were reviewed in the current 2026–2027 department catalogs; all nine publish three credits. The program elective cells remain blank but the exact course pages establish their credits.
